accepted.evidence: Turner 3818 explicitly lists Shumashti xareṭá “donkey” as an extension of khara. Buddruss xareṭa has the same animal sense and consonants; source accentuation is retained. Exact manually collated source row and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 1921 explicitly lists Shumashti wō “water” under udaká. Buddruss writes vō; the v/w notation difference is recorded, not silently normalized. Exact manually collated source row and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 3023 explicitly lists Shumashti kō̃ “arrow” under kā́ṇḍa. Buddruss kõ represents the same nasalized arrow stem with its source vowel notation. Exact manually collated source row and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 3440 explicitly lists Shumashti λoā̃lī “mulberry” in the *kr̥mukalī branch. Buddruss gives the same form and tree sense. Exact manually collated source row and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 43 explicitly lists Shumashti aĩċ “eye” under ákṣi. Buddruss aĩʦ uses a different affricate symbol for the same local eye word. Exact manually collated source row and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 2445 explicitly lists Shumashti ī̃c̣ “bear” under ŕ̥kṣa. Buddruss ĩʦ̣ shares the nasalized vowel and affricate stem; Turner notes taboo remodeling in the wider animal-name family. Exact manually collated source row and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 1872 explicitly lists Shumashti učä́nik “spring of water” under *utsadhānī. Buddruss ucānik has the same consonant pattern and spring/source sense. Exact manually collated source row and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 2892 explicitly lists Shumashti λā̆m “work” under kárman. Buddruss λăm has the same lateral onset and work sense. Exact manually collated source row and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.
